chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, raising it, said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: There is no pain more painful to the hearts than sins, and there is no fear more intense than death. What has passed is sufficient for reflection, and death is sufficient as an admonisher.

key_terms.الذُّنُوبِ: sins that spiritually harm and burden the heart
key_terms.الْقُلُوبِ: the hearts, meaning the inner spiritual center of the human being
key_terms.الْمَوْتِ: death, as the inevitable end of worldly life and a source of admonition
key_terms.تَفَكُّرًا: reflection and deep contemplation over what has passed
key_terms.وَاعِظًا: an admonisher; something that gives moral warning and instruction

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali عليه السلام describe the effect of sins on the heart and the lesson of death?
ai.summary: This saying of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام teaches that sins wound the heart more deeply than any outward pain, and that death is the most serious object of fear and reflection. It calls the listener to moral self-examination, to learn from what has already passed, and to take death itself as a constant admonition.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, raising it, said,

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘There is no pain more painful to the hearts than the sins, and there is no fear more intense than (fear of) the death, and suffice with what is past for pondering, and suffice with the death as a preaching’.
en.sarwar: 28. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus in a marfu’ manner from Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.)

who has said the following: “No pain is more painful to the heart than sins and there is no fear more intense than fear of death. Past experience is enough material for thinking and death is more than enough a preacher.”
